title: Chainsaw
summary: Sam's close-range cutting tool. Hold fire to keep attacking without spending ammunition.

sections.title: In the field
sections.text: The original NETRICSA entry describes a forestry tool repurposed for fighting monsters. Its short reach makes positioning essential.

sections.title: In the PC port
sections.text: Hold fire to keep cutting without consuming ammunition. The PC port doubles the original reach to 192 map units. Its running and stopping sounds follow the actual attack state.

coverage: The chainsaw is starting equipment; zero pickup records does not mean it is unavailable. The PC port deliberately increases its reach.

title: Schofield Pistol
summary: A reliable revolver and the first firearm introduced in the campaign.

sections.title: In the field
sections.text: NETRICSA presents the Schofield as Sam's dependable old-fashioned sidearm. A pistol pickup is available in the Upper Temple of Herkat.

sections.title: In the PC port
sections.text: Each shot hits immediately along the aim line. The pistol finishes its firing animation before returning to its ready pose.

title: Double Barrel Coach Gun
summary: A slow-firing shotgun built for close encounters.

sections.title: In the field
sections.text: The original briefing emphasizes the coach gun's short-range power. Its firing cycle leaves a pause between blasts.

sections.title: In the PC port
sections.text: A blast checks a central hit and two offset hits. It fires both cartridges when available, with a separate firing animation when only one cartridge remains.

title: Thompson Sub Machine Gun
summary: An automatic weapon for sustained fire against groups of enemies.

sections.title: In the field
sections.text: NETRICSA describes the Thompson as a classic trench sweeper suited to nearby and medium-range threats.

sections.title: In the PC port
sections.text: Holding fire produces repeated immediate hits while ammunition remains. Its firing sound stops when the attack ends, including after switching weapons or pausing.

title: Mini Gun
summary: A rotary gun that trades ammunition for sustained firepower.

sections.title: In the field
sections.text: The original tips call attention to its heavy ammunition use. It is introduced early in the Pyramid Entrance Maze.

sections.title: In the PC port
sections.text: Holding fire produces a continuous stream of immediate hits. The firing loop and the wind-down sound follow different stages of the weapon cycle.

title: Rocket Launcher
summary: Launches explosive projectiles with area damage.

sections.title: In the field
sections.text: The original description combines direct projectile damage with an explosion around the impact. Reloading separates each launch.

sections.title: PC behavior
sections.text: Player rockets travel independently after launch. Their trajectory follows the launch aim, including vertical mouse aim, rather than continuing to move with later changes to the player's view.

title: Rogue Prion Gun
summary: Turns eligible enemies against other enemies while their health drains away.

sections.title: In the field
sections.text: NETRICSA describes the weapon as disrupting Mental's control over his troops. The recovered effect changes target selection and applies periodic health drain; it is not a freeze weapon.

sections.title: PC behavior
sections.text: Shots leave along the sight line and continue independently. Converted living regular enemies receive the requested double-speed behavior and animation updates. Their projectiles and other actors retain their normal clocks.

title: Uni-Directional Microwave Transmitter
summary: A special blast weapon with a palette flash and a cooldown between attacks.

sections.title: In the field
sections.text: The original fiction describes a repurposed communications device that heats its targets. Its familiar pickup label is U.M.T.

sections.title: In the PC port
sections.text: The attack uses the original sector-based targeting checks and deals heavy damage to eligible regular enemies. It has a cooldown and excludes players and both bosses.

title: Time Strike
summary: Marks an enemy's position for a falling object from another time.

sections.title: In the field
sections.text: NETRICSA's explanation involves scientists sending heavy everyday objects back to Sam's recorded target coordinates. The effect captures a position rather than following the target indefinitely.

sections.title: PC behavior
sections.text: The falling effect lands, then explodes on its next update. The PC targeting policy requires an eligible living enemy; an invalid attempt completes the weapon gesture without spending ammunition. Tougher enemies can survive its original damage.

title: SBC Cannon
summary: Fires a large cannonball that can bounce off walls and pass through enemies.

sections.title: In the field
sections.text: The original NETRICSA entry highlights the cannonball's ricochets and ability to plow through a group.

sections.title: In the PC port
sections.text: Cannonballs can reflect from walls, penetrate targets and eventually explode. Hits retain credit for the player who fired the shot.

title: Beheaded Kamikaze
summary: An explosive pursuer that becomes dangerous when it closes the distance.

sections.title: In the field
sections.text: The original intel describes a reanimated attacker carrying bombs. Its cry provides an audible warning of the approaching threat.

sections.title: In the PC port
sections.text: Runs toward its target and detonates at close range. Its explosion damages nearby actors; defeating it also contributes to its scripted encounter group.

title: Sirian Werebull
summary: A charging beast whose close-range contact can knock Sam back.

sections.title: In the field
sections.text: NETRICSA recommends dodging the charge and taking advantage of the time it needs to turn for another approach.

sections.title: In the PC port
sections.text: Its close attack deals damage and pushes the target in the direction of impact. The charging sound warns of its approach.

title: Methug Soldier
summary: A floating soldier with a ranged bolt attack and harmful close contact.

sections.title: In the field
sections.text: The original intel describes its useless trailing legs and the bolt fired from its body. It is among the first enemies encountered in the campaign.

sections.title: In the PC port
sections.text: Bobs above the floor as it moves. It can hurt Sam on contact and attack with a projectile; attack and death animations run natively.

title: Methug Commander
summary: A compact hovering Methug variant with a dangerous contact attack.

sections.title: In the field
sections.text: NETRICSA describes a commander associated with other Methugs. Its eye and suspended body distinguish it from the soldier.

sections.title: In the PC port
sections.text: Attacks by contact. The recovered behavior contains no ranged attack, although the original NETRICSA description mentions a bolt fired from its eye.

title: Cyclops
summary: A mutated cyclopean attacker with prominent club-like arms.

sections.title: In the field
sections.text: The original intel emphasizes the danger of letting this fast-moving creature reach Sam.

sections.title: In the PC port
sections.text: Approaches its target, hurts Sam on contact and can fire a projectile. Its starting health is 100.

title: Bladder Beast
summary: A swollen Methug relative that threatens Sam with spit and close contact.

sections.title: In the field
sections.text: NETRICSA attributes its unusual movement to inflatable body sacs and describes a corrosive ranged attack.

sections.title: In the PC port
sections.text: Moves toward a target and can attack both on contact and with a projectile.

title: Aludran Arachnoid
summary: A scorpion-like ranged enemy that can threaten Sam before he reaches it.

sections.title: In the field
sections.text: The original dossier describes an armed, many-legged hybrid that prefers to open fire from a distance.

sections.title: In the PC port
sections.text: Can launch projectiles from a distance and hurt Sam on contact. Movement, attacks and death behavior are implemented natively.

title: Aludran Reptiloid
summary: A tough projectile attacker often encountered as a distant sentry.

sections.title: In the field
sections.text: The original briefing describes rapid acid-missile attacks and recommends heavy weapons against this durable enemy.

sections.title: In the PC port
sections.text: Its attack animation triggers a projectile launch. When sufficiently high above Sam, it uses a different aiming behavior rather than its ordinary approach.

title: Hermit Crabuloid
summary: A shelled enemy that alternates between exposed movement and hiding.

sections.title: In the field
sections.text: NETRICSA describes the shell as protection and directs attention to the vulnerable body revealed while the creature is active.

sections.title: In the PC port
sections.text: Burrows, hides and emerges again according to its distance from the target. It can also jump during a close approach.

title: Gunrilla
summary: A heavily armed gorilla mutant with a large projectile weapon grafted onto its body.

sections.title: In the field
sections.text: The original description portrays a slow, heavily armed opponent that is dangerous both at range and up close.

sections.title: In the PC port
sections.text: Fires cannonball projectiles and has a strong close-range attack. Its starting health is 150.

title: Sirian Sphinx
summary: The Egyptian chapter's boss, combining projectile volleys with scripted reinforcements.

sections.title: Encounter
sections.text: The Sphinx has its own health gauge, battle music and scripted encounter. Its controller alternates attack cycles with reinforcement phases.

sections.title: PC port coverage
sections.text: The sixth campaign level has a normal-input completion with earned inventory and native boss combat. Summoning phases also have separate controller and integration tests.

title: Wolfiator
summary: An armored wolf-like boss commanding the final Roman encounter.

sections.title: Encounter
sections.text: The original intel describes a towering enemy with a plumed helmet and summoned minions. Its recovered controller combines five-shot volleys with alternating scripted reinforcement phases.

sections.title: PC port coverage
sections.text: The boss controller and its native integration are implemented and tested. Natural progression through the final campaign level remains to be validated; those tests do not yet establish a complete playable final encounter.
